problem.title_en: Does every prime modulus have a relatively small prime primitive root?

items.citation:
# Candidate observation

## English

This candidate observation is associated with [JSP-000818 — Does every prime modulus have a relatively small prime primitive root?](https://github.com/TheJustinSunPrize/awards/blob/main/problems/catalog-0801-0900.md#JSP-000818). It publishes `Statement.lean` and `Proof.lean` for a complete, machine-checked Lean formalization of a finite instance table of the catalog question: for each odd prime `p ≤ 19`, the least prime primitive root modulo `p` is explicitly verified. The table is `2` for `p = 3, 5, 11, 13, 19` and `3` for `p = 7, 17`. For each pair `(p, g)` the formal statement verifies three components: primality of `p`; that `g` is a primitive root modulo `p`, phrased directly as the multiplicative order condition `g ^ (p - 1) = 1` in `ZMod p` with no smaller positive power equal to `1` (with companion theorems repackaging each instance in Mathlib's `IsPrimitiveRoot` semantics as `IsPrimitiveRoot (g : ZMod p) (p - 1)`); and that `g` is the least such prime (every prime `q < g` fails the same order condition; vacuous for `g = 2`, and checking `q = 2` for `g = 3`, whose orders modulo 7 and 17 are 3 and 8, not 6 and 16).

**Scope boundary:** this observation records only the finite, fully verified instance table for the odd primes `p ≤ 19` (with `p = 2` degenerate: the only unit of `ZMod 2` is `1`, not a prime, so it has no prime primitive root at all). It makes no assertion for arbitrary prime moduli and does not touch the smallness question of the catalog problem (whether every prime modulus has a prime primitive root bounded by, e.g., some fixed power of `log p`). It does not resolve the catalogued open problem, which remains Open, and makes no award claim.

The formal source is pinned to the public repository [Yaohua-Leo/jsp-000818-lean](https://github.com/Yaohua-Leo/jsp-000818-lean) at commit `4abdf2862a5caa141715af3560f48154a78ec7c6` on branch `main`. A local Lean compilation was run with the pinned toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc2` and Mathlib `v4.35.0-rc2`: `lake env lean JSP000818.lean` produces zero errors and zero warnings, and `#print axioms` for every theorem in the file reports only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` — no `sorryAx` or any other axiom, and no `sorry`, `admit`, or `native_decide` anywhere. These compiler results are reproducibility evidence for the stated formal theorems; they are not official JSP verification or award admission.

The catalog entry records "No later than 1965 (bibliographic evidence)" with no publication details, so the `posed.citation` field points to the catalog entry itself as the source of record rather than to an external publication.

The candidate remains under verification. No award decision, recipient identity, solver or formalizer credit, payment, or official verification is asserted.

## English

No recipient is identified in this preliminary observation. It makes no recipient, award, payment, or identity claim. For attribution of the formalization only: formalization author Yaohua-Leo, AI-assisted via ZCode (GLM); mathematical credit for the catalogued question and for the underlying classical facts (Gauss's primitive root theorem and standard tables of least prime primitive roots) belongs to the public number-theory record of JSP-000818.
